subject.title: [Bug]: Concurrent allow-always approvals silently lose allowlist entries (last-write-wins race in exec-approvals.json)

question: Should maintainers adopt or replace the shared guarded-write/CAS fix path for exec approval stale writes, or sponsor a narrower allow-always-only fix for this issue?
rationale: The bug affects command-execution approval state and overlaps an unresolved security-sensitive stale-writeback PR, so starting another automated fix branch without choosing the persistence boundary could create competing security-state semantics.

options.title: Adopt or replace shared guarded write
options.body: Use a single locked/CAS merge primitive for allow-always and usage metadata writes, refresh it on current main, and require security-focused regression proof before merge.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow allow-always repair
options.body: Limit the fix to concurrent allow-always entry persistence if maintainers want to defer the broader node metadata stale-writeback track.

options.title: Wait for the security PR track
options.body: Keep this issue open while the node stale-writeback PR decides the shared persistence primitive, then close or repair this issue from that outcome.

recommendation.title: Adopt or replace shared guarded write
recommendation.body: Use a single locked/CAS merge primitive for allow-always and usage metadata writes, refresh it on current main, and require security-focused regression proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They have recent merged history in the same remote exec approval and persistence boundary and are the strongest routing candidate from the code history.
